data.title: N Prisoners in Hats
data.solution:
import sys
import math

hats = []

N = int(input())
for i in range(N):
    H = int(input())
    hats.append(H)

guesses = [0] * N
    
# Step 1: Prisoner N acts as the anchor.
# They count the black hats strictly in front of them (indices 0 to N-2)
# This means slicing up to index N-1
black_hats_seen_by_N = sum(hats[:N-1])

# Shout 1 if odd, 0 if even
prisoner_N_guess = 1 if (black_hats_seen_by_N % 2 != 0) else 0

# Array to store the final output guesses from Prisoner N down to Prisoner 1
guesses = [0] * N
guesses[0] = prisoner_N_guess

# Track the parity of black hats remaining in front of the current prisoner.
# Initially, this is the total parity announced by Prisoner N.
running_parity = prisoner_N_guess

# Step 2: Process Prisoner N-1 down to Prisoner 1
# i represents the index of the current prisoner in the hats array (from N-2 down to 0)
# guess_idx is the position in the output string (moving from 1 up to N-1)
guess_idx = 1
for i in range(N - 2, -1, -1):
    # The current prisoner counts the black hats they can see in front of them
    black_hats_in_front = sum(hats[:i])
    front_parity = 1 if (black_hats_in_front % 2 != 0) else 0
    
    # Their own hat is the difference between the expected total parity 
    # and the parity of the hats they see ahead
    own_hat = running_parity ^ front_parity
    guesses[guess_idx] = own_hat
    
    # The next prisoner knows this person's hat color, 
    # so the expected parity for the remaining line updates
    running_parity = front_parity
    guess_idx += 1

# Print the guesses as a single space-delimited string
print(*(guesses))
data.statement:
A warden lines up [[N]] prisoners in a single-file line. Each prisoner faces forward. Prisoner [[N]] is at the back of the line and can see everyone in front of them. Prisoner 1 is at the very front and can see no one. The warden places either a Black hat ({{1}}) or a White hat ({{0}}) on each prisoner's head. No prisoner can see their own hat. 

Starting from the back (Prisoner [[N]]) and moving to the front, each prisoner must guess the color of their own hat by shouting out either "Black" or "White". If a prisoner guesses correctly, they go free. If they guess wrong, they stay in prison. Every prisoner can hear the guesses of the people behind them. Before the game starts, the prisoners can meet to agree on a strategy. 

Before any other prisoner can guess, prisoner [[N]] must act as the anchor for the team. Prisoner [[N]]'s guess is strictly treated as a signaling mechanism. Prisoner [[N]] must shout "Black" if they see an odd number of Black hats in front of them or "White" if they see an even number of Black hats in front of them. If Prisoner [[N]]'s guess does not accurately match the odd/even parity of the hats ahead of them, the entire strategy is disqualified instantly, and all prisoners remain in prison.


Write an algorithm that acts as the strategy for the prisoners. Your strategy must save at least [[N]] - 1 prisoners.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

A warden lines up N prisoners in a single-file line. Each prisoner faces forward. Prisoner N is at the back of the line and can see everyone in front of them. Prisoner 1 is at the very front and can see no one. The warden places either a Black hat (1) or a White hat (0) on each prisoner's head. No prisoner can see their own hat.

Starting from the back (Prisoner N) and moving to the front, each prisoner must guess the color of their own hat by shouting out either "Black" or "White". If a prisoner guesses correctly, they go free. If they guess wrong, they stay in prison. Every prisoner can hear the guesses of the people behind them. Before the game starts, the prisoners can meet to agree on a strategy.

Before any other prisoner can guess, prisoner N must act as the anchor for the team. Prisoner N's guess is strictly treated as a signaling mechanism. Prisoner N must shout "Black" if they see an odd number of Black hats in front of them or "White" if they see an even number of Black hats in front of them. If Prisoner N's guess does not accurately match the odd/even parity of the hats ahead of them, the entire strategy is disqualified instantly, and all prisoners remain in prison.


Write an algorithm that acts as the strategy for the prisoners. Your strategy must save at least N - 1 prisoners.
Input
Line 1: An integer N for the number of prisoners.

Next N lines: An integer H which is 1 or 0 where 1 represents a Black hat and 0 represents a White hat. The array is ordered from front to back (Index 0 is Prisoner 1, Index N-1 is Prisoner N.
Output
The guesses made by the prisoners, from Prisoner N down to Prisoner 1 represented as a space delimited string of 0s and 1s on a single line.
Constraints
3 <= N <= 100
Example
Input
3
1
0
1
Output
1 0 1
